label: Squarish-shell 2-STOREY 2BR / 2 baths, L-SHAPED LANDING STAIR, hall-less ground floor — same hall-less parti as the rear-corner straight-stair sibling, but the stair turns 90 degrees at a quarter landing instead of running straight: boards off the great room's south wall, turns, and arrives into the landing hall's east wall. Open great room across the full front, kitchen + T&B in a rear wet bay. Upstairs, the squarish signature: BOTH bedrooms side-by-side at the front with street-facing windows, landing hall behind them, second T&B at the rear near the wet stack. Canonical 9.5x9.5 lot (true floor ~9.2x9.2), 0-warning band through ~14x14.

GF: T&B doors into the great room — hall-less GF, the great room IS the circulation; door-placement scoring keeps it off the entry sightline
GF: L-landing stair boards off the great room on its SOUTH wall (author-fixed — a turning stair's boarding/arrival walls aren't a solver-chosen ascent axis, see Adjacency.stair_wall)
GF: T&B shares a plumbing wall with the kitchen — single GF wet bay at the rear; kitchen keeps its rear service door
VERTICAL circulation edge: flight and stairwell opening occupy the identical rectangle on their floors (rect-equality in the solver, graph connectivity for validation)
2F: the landing hall meets the stairwell on its EAST wall — a 90-degree turn from the south-boarding wall, via the quarter landing
2F: master door off the landing hall
2F: second bedroom door off the landing hall
2F: second T&B doors off the landing hall

soft_proximities.note: 2F: pull the upper T&B toward the rear stair corner — lands it near the GF wet bay (kitchen + bath1 share the rear band), shortening the vertical plumbing run. Soft only: cross-floor wet-stack alignment isn't a hard v2 constraint yet.

zone_split.note: 2F-only geometric partition (all listed rooms are storey 2, per the multi-storey zone_split rule): both bedrooms hold the FRONT band — the squarish signature, side-by-side street-facing windows — with the T&B strictly behind the split line. 'public_rooms' here is the mechanical 'other side of the split' list, not a zoning claim; hall2 and stairwell float.

lot_adjustment_profiles.name: stair_l_landing_geometry
lot_adjustment_profiles.rationale: ALWAYS-ON (the 99999 trigger). L-landing bounding-box sizing per the stair-types research: hard tier ~2.15x2.15 m (two ~1.4 m legs + a 0.75 m landing), preferred tier ~3.2x3.2 m. min_least_dim_m floors BOTH sides (near-square, unlike a straight stair's thin-rectangle profile); max_greatest_dim_m keeps it from stretching into an elongated rectangle that would defeat the point of the turn. set_max_area_sqm=10.5 is required, not optional — the 'stairs' room-catalog's own preferred_area_sqm ceiling (4.5, tuned for a straight stair) collides with min_area_sqm=4.5 into an exact-equality area target with no valid grid-integer solution once both dims also floor at 2.1 m (confirmed via factor-pair arithmetic: 1800 grid-unit² has no factor pair both >=42) — genuinely infeasible at every lot size, not a sizing-tightness issue. The common_bath caps are unchanged from the straight-stair sibling.

notes: 2-STOREY squarish catalog topology — L-SHAPED LANDING STAIR, hall-less GF
(authored 2026-07-23, the catalog's first non-straight stair type; sibling
of 2s_2br_sq_rear_stair_bath_gr, same room program and hall-less parti,
differing ONLY in the stair's own shape).
Why an L-landing stair, and why squarish: the straight-stair sibling
needs a >= 3.5 m run in ONE direction (15 risers x 250 mm treads).
L-landing folds that same run into a near-square ~2.1-3.6 m bounding box
by turning 90 degrees at a quarter landing partway up — trading a little
floor area (the landing) for NOT needing 3.5 m of spare depth or width in
a single axis. Squarish is the shell this actually helps: a narrow shell
already has depth to spare for a straight run (folding it buys nothing);
a squarish shell's balanced width/depth is exactly where a near-square
stair footprint fits naturally instead of eating into whichever axis is
scarcer.

Adjacency.stair_wall in solver/topology.py).
Structure/override choices (each per an established convention):
- zone_split is a 2F-ONLY horizontal partition pinning both bedrooms
to the front band with bath2 behind — the side-by-side-bedrooms
signature, stated as one split line instead of anchor lists (the
3BR catalog's over-constrained-anchors trap; only the stair is
anchored, single-member list, the proven-safe pattern).
- zone_balance_rooms counts the whole upper floor minus stairwell as
the private wing — same reasoning as the narrow hall-less sibling:
bedrooms-alone can't outweigh a full-width GF great room + kitchen.
- Hall-less GF: at 36 m²/floor the great room is the circulation
(stair boards off it, bath1 doors into it) per the compact
convention; a _hall sibling for larger squarish lots (with
fallback_below_buildable_sqm routing back here) is future work.
- soft proximity bath2->stairwell pulls the upper bath toward the
rear corner, near the GF wet bay, to shorten the vertical plumbing
run (cross-floor wet-stack alignment is still soft-only in v2).
Naming note: the `bath` token undercounts the program (two common
baths, one per floor) — kept consistent with the 2s narrow siblings
pending the 2s naming-convention pass.
